observation.visible_scene: Top-down view of a plain white surface. A pair of hands (gray sweater cuffs) manipulates a flat triangular lattice built from shiny metallic magnetic spheres: three ball-chain edges joined at the vertices, with internal diagonal braces and a small triangular hole in the center. In the upper-right corner a separate chain/cluster of the same spheres lies on the table and does not move during the clip. The background and the upper-right chain stay in fixed screen positions, so the camera is stationary.
visible_changes: For the first portion (frames 1–17) both hands pinch the top vertex of the triangular structure, holding it roughly steady with only small finger adjustments; the triangle keeps apex-up orientation.
Around frames 18–20 the hands release the apex and slide outward to grip the left and right sides/vertices, leaving the top vertex free.
From roughly frames 21–33 the structure is held by its two lower side vertices, orientation still apex-up, with minor positional settling.

In the final portion (frames ~34–41) the hands rotate the whole triangle in-plane so the apex swings from pointing up toward pointing left (counterclockwise), while the grips shift to match the new orientation.
The upper-right sphere chain and the white background remain static throughout, confirming the observed motion is object/hand movement rather than camera movement.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the triangular lattice was assembled before the clip began.
What the hands do with the structure after the excerpt ends (further rotation, disassembly, etc.).
Whether the lattice is fully rigid or flexes slightly under the grip.
uncertain_details: Exact rotation angle and whether a small lateral translation accompanies the rotation.
Whether the central hole and internal braces change shape (deformation) or only change apparent orientation due to in-plane rotation.
Specular highlights on the spheres are reflections, not separate objects.
